events.label: Cultivation and its consequences, from about 12,000 years ago.
events.description: Farming produced surplus, storage, property, hierarchy, writing, money and debt. Time became the calendar of the harvest: the same work in the same field every season. Institutions grew to manage strangers who had to trust each other: temples, granaries, ledgers, kings, courts, and much later banks with double-entry books.

events.label: Programmable money: from the 2008 crisis and the first cryptocurrency to smart contracts,…
events.description: A ledger nobody owns, that never closes, where code replaces the clerk. It promised to route around the old institutions and instead reproduced most of their temptations at machine speed, in public, around the clock.

events.label: The global institutional order built mostly after 1944: a world of international money, t…
events.description: The global institutions people live inside took shape within roughly the last fifty to eighty years: post-war monetary agreements, the international lenders, card networks, interbank messaging, the floating dollar after 1971. They are younger than many living grandparents, and most people who depend on them have never seen how they work.

nodes.text: The human author's brief (2026-09-25, supplied by the human in chat, verbatim): "Write me a novel of about 11,000 words in twelve parts from this idea of mine. Choose everything else yourself." The idea follows verbatim. Write a story about someone born into a world they know nothing about. It's a "blue pill" world: comfortable, familiar, and predictable. They know the people around them, and every week is pretty much the same, stuck in the 9-to-5 routine. Then, somewhere along the line, something strange happens. A "white rabbit" appears: a sign, a stranger, an opportunity that doesn't fit into their ordinary life. Our protagonist is faced with a difficult choice. Human curiosity is powerful, and after years of monotony, they're tired enough to follow it. They choose the unknown. The story should echo the most iconic imagery in pop culture, moments everyone recognizes, like Neo touchin…

Collaboration agreement, read from the human's own message (no intake questions were needed because the message settles both choices). Initial settings: the human supplied the idea, about 11,000 words and twelve parts, and delegated everything else ('Choose everything else yourself'). Involvement: autonomous writing and modeling within that brief, carried out in rounds of about fifteen minutes; at the end of each round the LLM stops, reports what it has made and what it would do next, and waits until the human says to continue. These stops are progress updates, not approval checkpoints: the human reserved no creative decision. One operational decision came from the human: when the session opened in the parent folder, the human chose this run folder (meaning-model-rabbit-hole-run-2026-09-25/novel) as the working folder at 19:17 CEST. All creative choices recorded after this are the LLM's…

Name candidates for the invented author persona, from the random seed word 'fade' (life_story_structure_explore, name mode): Faye Titcombe, Jade Kempster, Dale Webb. Etymological remarks are ordinary English associations, not invented derivations.

Selected under delegation (LLM choice, not a human decision): the invented author persona is Faye Titcombe, born 1979 in Swindon, who publishes under that name. Reason: the name fits a working-class Swindon family in 1979, carries the seed's two private senses (fading chalk that must be scoured; betting against the crowd) without symbolism on the surface, and is not a known author's name. Jade Kempster fits the year less well; Dale Webb is flatter and fits the chosen life less.

End of round 1 (19:28 CEST). Made: story model r0 (deep-time frame, protagonist scaffold), story graph, brief and agreement records, author persona Faye Titcombe named and her life registered as its own model (faye-titcombe-life r0). nodes.title: event:event.profile.faye.person.faye.life in model faye-titcombe-life
nodes.text: Invented life of Faye Titcombe from her birth in Swindon in March 1979 to September 2026, when she is finishing this novel. Her life runs between two kinds of time: the deep time of the Wiltshire downs she studied and the batch cycles of the payments office where she worked.

Author model: Faye Titcombe, an invented persona (fictional_author), writing this novel in 2025-2026. Her life (faye-titcombe-life r2) produces six writing dispositions: band vision (offices and chat servers seen as forager bands), mechanism clarity (exact, brief explanations of how the money moves), walking beside (no warnings, no punishment, no absolution), wry comedy as a way of carrying shame, a landscape of chalk and stones with three clocks running at once, and respect for the dignity of routine. Each has a counterweight recorded with it. All basis is invented except one labelled interpretation. Composition point and reasons are recorded as basis b.composition; her life model is faye-titcombe-life revision 2 (model 4d462a80d15a0f0882d4d4926aafd99c06daff1f4fba95970e9969486919167e).

nodes.title: event:ev.faye.composition in model faye-titcombe-life
nodes.text: Faye writes in the evenings after guiding at the stones, at the kitchen table in north Swindon. She is four years from her own fall and far enough to laugh at parts of it.

nodes.title: event:ev.faye.learn_beside in model faye-titcombe-life
nodes.text: Instead of forbidding it, Faye asks her daughter to show her how it works. They sit with it on Sunday evenings; Faye explains what she knows about order books and liquidity and, in pieces, what happened to her in 2022. Her daughter keeps a small balance and starts asking better questions. Faye starts the novel the same autumn, writing as someone walking beside a person who will go in anyway.

nodes.title: referent:referent.profile.faye.person.faye in model faye-titcombe-life
nodes.text: Faye Titcombe, invented author persona: one English woman born 1979 in Swindon, Wiltshire

author_reader: The book comes out of Faye Titcombe's invented life: a railway-works child who learned that routine is someone else's to end, an archaeologist of the first gatherings, eighteen years inside the payments batch, a fall into decentralized finance in 2020-2022 that she understood and could not stop. She writes it in 2025-2026 beside a fifteen-year-old daughter who has just found a trading app. The story presses the fear of being left behind, the fear that a safe life is someone else's to end, the longing for more world, and the shame of knowing better.

candidates: Three candidate worlds from Faye's life: The Exceptions Queue (a Swindon payments clerk handed twelve words by an engineer who built the old machine), Twelve Words (a warehouse picker finds a stranger's wallet) and The Pension (a claims handler of fifty-eight). Chosen under delegation: The Exceptions Queue, keeping the twelve words and an older person's late wonder from the others.

Faye's open decision was drawn, not chosen: cut.faye.2025.daughter_app.response (faye-titcombe-life r1, 65cbe4fe) with seed 'rabbit-hole-run/faye/daughter-app/2025-09', u=0.2055, realized learn_it_beside_her (first draw, no reroll). The draw could not be recorded in a graph bound to her model because her life model has no graph of its own, so the full draw result is kept here and the continuation (ev.faye.learn_beside) carries a realizes_forecast relation in r2 (4d462a80). Remaining author-life questions and why they stay: the nine slow processes are described on their Events and opened where the causality runs through them (body and partnership in the 2022 adaptation, work in the redundancy arc); further opening would not change the voice. Name candidates for the protagonist from the random seed word 'ear': Kieran Hale, Tom Earley, Ryan Hearn.

Selected under delegation (LLM choice): the protagonist is Kieran Hale, born 1990 in Swindon, called Kez by colleagues. The name is ordinary for his year and town, and the seed's sense of listening fits a man whose job is to hear a scam in a stranger's voice, without symbolism on the surface. Tom Earley reads as a pun; Ryan Hearn is flatter.
Name candidates for the retired engineer from the random seed word 'branch': Barbara Ashby, Brenda Ash, Margaret Lyne.

Selected under delegation (LLM choice): the engineer is Barbara Ashby, born 1953 in Swindon, who insists on 'Barbara, never Babs'. The name fits her year, is distinct from Kieran Hale and Faye Titcombe, and the seed's senses (bank branch, branch line, code branch, fork) are private resonances with her life, not surface symbolism.
Name candidates for Kieran's partner from the random seed word 'autumn': Laura Russell, Amber Price, Hannah Russell.

Selected under delegation (LLM choice): Kieran's partner is Laura Russell, born 1991, an intensive-care nurse; Kieran calls her Lor. Ordinary for her year and distinct from the other names; the seed's autumn stays a private resonance.

End of round 2 (19:42 CEST). Made: Faye's life r1-r2 (change arcs, wants under an inner root, places, long developments, concepts and realizations, outlook and threat Cuts, a drawn decision: learn_it_beside_her), her author model (author.model.faye), the author_reader stage with five buttons, the candidates stage (The Exceptions Queue chosen), and names for the three principals: Kieran Hale (Kez), Barbara Ashby, Laura Russell (Lor). Next: name the building society and the chat server; the opening stage with the era marked real (documentary cutoff about 2023) and each real fact used recorded as a report with its source (the March 2020 lockdown and crash, the 2020 yield-farming summer, the November 2021 peak, the May 2022 stablecoin collapse, the June 2022 lending freezes, the November 2022 exchange collapse; the 2019 scam-reimbursement code and 2020 payee checks; banks' limits on crypto …
Name candidates for Kieran's building society from the random seed word 'heart': the White Hart Building Society, Hearth and Home Building Society, Heartland Building Society.

Selected under delegation (LLM choice): Kieran works for the White Hart Building Society (staff say 'the Hart'), an invented mutual founded in 1868 by Swindon railwaymen meeting at a White Hart inn, head office and payments operations in west Swindon. It stands in for the town's real mutuals, which stay unnamed. A white animal sits in the old institution's name without anyone in the story remarking on it.
